description: Publish responses for each activation result, what each one means, and the lines `userland apps publish` prints for it. `cli/tests/cli.test.ts` runs every case. The meanings are the ones every Userland client must agree on (dwrtz/userland#286): `live` says whether the new release serves, `serving` says which release the app's address shows now (`this_release`, `previous_release`, or `nothing`), and `address_restricted` says whether billing or the plan has turned the address off. A publish returns only live, pending_secrets, requires_migration, or failed; `inactive` appears only in release lists.

cases.name: live_billing_restricted

reasons: Release is live but canonical serving is restricted by billing or plan state.

stdout_lines: The release is live, but the app's web address is turned off for now: the account's billing or plan is restricting this app, so visitors can't open it.
activation_reasons=Release is live but canonical serving is restricted by billing or plan state.

cases.name: pending_secrets_first_publish

reasons: Required secret STRIPE_SECRET_KEY is not set.
Required secret OPENAI_API_KEY is not set.

stdout_lines: Stored, not live: this release is not serving yet.
Why: Required secret STRIPE_SECRET_KEY is not set.
Why: Required secret OPENAI_API_KEY is not set.
No release of this app is live yet, so https://app_fixture.apps.userland.fun/ does not show it yet.
Next: printf '%s' "$VALUE" | userland apps secrets set app_fixture STRIPE_SECRET_KEY
or the owner adds it at https://console.example.test/apps/app_fixture/settings?add-key=STRIPE_SECRET_KEY
Next: printf '%s' "$VALUE" | userland apps secrets set app_fixture OPENAI_API_KEY
or the owner adds it at https://console.example.test/apps/app_fixture/settings?add-key=OPENAI_API_KEY
Next: userland apps publish examples/hello-static --app app_fixture
activation_reasons=Required secret STRIPE_SECRET_KEY is not set.; Required secret OPENAI_API_KEY is not set.
